actions_performed: read-only SHA256 comparison of all 103 frozen candidate artifacts
read-only in-memory schema, canonical Rule hash, chronology, binding and uniqueness probes

evidence: A dedicated domain-rule-human-approval schema exists and requires schema version, human producer, approval method, procedural identity assurance, human owner, Rule ID/version/canonical hash, source type/reference/hash/verification time, approval time/scope/effective time and verification method.

validate-task.mjs does not load or apply domain-rule-approval.schema.json. Its approval-record path checks only artifact classification/provenance literals, Rule ID/version/canonical hash and the three approval-record timestamps.

The confirmation path does not require approval-record human_owner to equal Rule human_owner, approval-record approved_at/scope/effective_from to equal the Rule authority fields, or approval-record source reference/hash and verification method to bind to verified authority evidence.

A read-only in-memory probe produced zero Rule-schema errors, zero domain-approval-schema errors and zero validateDomainApprovalRecord errors while owner, approval scope, effective time, source reference and source hash all disagreed between the otherwise valid approval record and Rule authority record.

Because the approval artifact bytes can still match authority.source_hash and be classified authoritative, these mismatches can survive validateConfirmedDomainRule and allow a confirmed Rule to participate in applicable_rules with false owner, source, scope, effective or verification claims. This is an in-contract incorrect GO, not merely the accepted residual limitation of procedural identity assurance.

read_only_commands: rg -n "validateConfirmedDomainRule|approval provenance|approval does not bind|approval chronology" .codex/scripts/validate-task.mjs

findings.impact: A hash-bound human approval record can authorize a confirmed Rule while the registry claims a different owner, source, approval scope, effective time or verification basis. The Candidate Governance Review Gate must remain NO-GO.

evidence: findManifestArtifacts scans every Task manifest but uses Array.find inside each manifest, so it returns at most one matching artifact per manifest even when that manifest contains the same approval_artifact_id more than once.
validateConfirmedDomainRule then accepts artifacts.length === 1 as global uniqueness. Two same-ID entries in one non-current Task manifest are therefore observed as one.

validateArtifactIdentities is applied only to the Task currently being validated. The approval-source Task manifest found during Domain confirmation is parsed but is not independently schema- or identity-validated by findManifestArtifacts.

A read-only in-memory probe of the exact per-manifest find algorithm observed two matching entries but exposed one authoritative match to the caller. This can produce an incorrect GO despite a non-unique approval identity.
findings.impact: The mechanism cannot prove that approval_artifact_id identifies exactly one filed authority artifact across all Task manifests, so ambiguous or forged approval identity can be accepted.

conditions.condition: Apply domain-rule-approval.schema.json to every referenced approval artifact and fail closed unless record and Rule authority agree on human owner, Rule ID/version/RULE-CORE-V1 hash, source type/reference/hash/verification time, approval time/scope/effective time and verification method.
conditions.completion_criterion: Isolated negative fixtures for each missing or mismatched binding return validation-error exit 1, while one fully bound procedural human approval succeeds.

conditions.condition: Replace per-manifest first-match lookup with complete artifact-ID collection, validate artifact identity uniqueness in every searched manifest and require exactly one authoritative domain-rule-human-approval match.
conditions.completion_criterion: A duplicate approval ID within one current or historical Task manifest is rejected before Rule confirmation, and a single unique approval remains accepted.

conditions.condition: After remediation, freeze a new immutable candidate baseline and obtain a fresh independent read-only Railway Domain Review without confirming any maintenance Rule.
conditions.completion_criterion: All Domain authority checks pass against the newly frozen candidate and the Reviewer records no blocking authority finding.

decisions_required.decision_deadline_or_trigger: Before any Migration 320 business approval or execution.

domain_checks.evidence: All 103 frozen candidate artifacts match review-baseline-before SHA256 values; manifest actual and expected SHA256 are both 7F234EAA894454AD46AD5A24469A87AB6E11F26F01218607397BE1FE4CE3335C.

validate-task.mjs:171-176 requires one authoritative artifact typed domain-rule-human-approval whose parsed record declares artifact_type=domain-rule-human-approval, producer_type=human and procedural identity assurance.
The dedicated schema is present in the candidate but absent from validate-task.mjs schema loading and is not applied to parsed approval records.

Record-to-Rule equality checks are absent for human_owner, source reference/hash, approval scope, effective time and verification method; the read-only mismatch probe was accepted by the shared Domain approval control.

governance-controls.mjs:61-64 canonically hashes rule_id, version, statement, applies_when, prohibited, verification, enforcement and scope. Read-only mutation probes confirmed every listed component invalidates the old approval hash.

validate-task.mjs:178-179 and governance-controls.mjs:70-71 enforce source_verified_at < approved_at <= effective_from and reject missing, invalid, equal or reversed record timestamps. However, the valid record timestamps are not required to equal the Rule approval/effective fields, which is part of blocking finding A4-DOMAIN-AUTHORITY-BINDING-001.

UNVERIFIED, report, implementation, migration, test or health/report evidence cannot independently confirm a Rule because a VERIFIED human-approval source and a unique authoritative domain-rule-human-approval artifact are required.
Per-manifest Array.find hides same-manifest duplicates from the global artifacts.length === 1 test.

No role in agent-path-policy.yaml has a write path to .codex/domain/** or permission for domain-rule-human-approval artifacts; Railway Domain Reviewer has no write paths and explicitly cannot confirm a Rule. The policy is commit-time and not runtime isolation, and QA lacks an explicit confirm-domain-rule prohibition, but QA still has no domain registry write path or permitted approval artifact type.

The model explicitly declares human_identity_assurance=procedural and does not claim cryptographic or OS-authenticated identity. This residual boundary is recorded as a risk and is not itself a blocker.
validate-task.mjs:197-198 programmatically recomputes confirmed Rules. The filed registry declares 0, the read-only recomputation is 0 and all six Rules are proposed; zero confirmed is legal.

WO-P-C-LINK-001, WO-C-SHORTAGE-001 and COMPAT-M320-001 remain candidate_rules and proposed. Railway Domain outcome is NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION, the three Migration 320 blockers remain filed and calculated/overall gates remain NO-GO.

A read-only lifecycle projection using the filed generated_at exactly matched phase-status.json and kept Candidate Review, commit preparation, commit execution and Migration 320 gates NO-GO. The filed projection intentionally remains pre-A4 with a4_started=false until a later authorized lifecycle update.

residual_risks.statement: Procedural human identity is a declared claim boundary rather than cryptographic actor authentication; this is not an independent blocker but must not be described as authenticated identity proof.
Commit-time role policy is not OS/runtime isolation. It prevents no filed Rule promotion by policy but cannot independently attribute who typed a producer_type=human record.

The current registry is non-authoritative and safe from immediate application because all six Rules remain proposed; the blocking authority defects become reachable when a confirmed Rule is introduced.
This Review determines only the Domain portion of the Candidate Governance Review Gate. It does not authorize Session B, staging, commit, release or Migration 320 execution.

candidate_review_gate_implication.reason: Two blocking Domain authority findings permit an in-contract incorrect GO for mismatched or non-unique approval authority.
